---
title: "Merge Census Line-Vintage Splits in NJ (103rd-107th) and TX (105th-107th) From Issue #36"
format: html
editor: source
---

## Overview

[Issue #36](https://github.com/JeffreyBLewis/congressional-district-boundaries/issues/36)
asks about two apparent mid-cycle boundary changes in this collection for
which no redistricting is documented anywhere:

- New Jersey between the 105th and 106th Congress
  (`New Jersey_103_to_105.geojson` vs. `New Jersey_106_to_107.geojson`), and
- Texas between the 106th and 107th Congress
  (`Texas_105_to_106.geojson` vs. `Texas_107_to_107.geojson`).

Neither is a real change of plan. Starting with the 103rd Congress this
collection takes its shapes directly from the Census Bureau's congressional
district files, and between these Congresses the Census re-digitized the
underlying TIGER line work (and realigned coastlines and state lines). The
original project database kept a separate per-Congress shape whenever the
Census file changed at all, and `R/dedup.R`'s 0.99 intersection-over-union
merge rule did not re-join them, because the sliver differences push the
small urban districts (NJ District 13, TX Districts 6, 18, and 20) just
under 0.99.

The historical record agrees:

- Census's own documentation of the 106th Congress files lists only New
  York, North Carolina, and Virginia as having redistricted for the 106th
  Congress; the 103rd-Congress districts otherwise stayed in effect through
  Census 2000.
- Texas's legislature never replaced the 1996 interim plan drawn in
  *Vera v. Bush*; when it missed the court's June 30, 1997 deadline, the
  court left the interim plan in place indefinitely (*Vera v. Bush*,
  980 F. Supp. 251 (S.D. Tex. 1997)), so the plan used for the 1996
  election was also used in 1998 and 2000.

This patch documents the evidence and then merges each pair into a single
file: `New Jersey_103_to_107.geojson` and `Texas_105_to_107.geojson`.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
sf_use_s2(FALSE)
```

```{r}
read_cd <- function(fn) {
  st_read(file.path("../../GeoJson", fn), quiet = TRUE) |>
    mutate(district = as.integer(district)) |>
    arrange(district)
}
nj_a <- read_cd("New Jersey_103_to_105.geojson")
nj_b <- read_cd("New Jersey_106_to_107.geojson")
tx_a <- read_cd("Texas_105_to_106.geojson")
tx_b <- read_cd("Texas_107_to_107.geojson")
```

## Characterizing the differences

A real redistricting moves whole blocks or precincts between a handful of
districts and leaves the rest untouched. A change of line vintage instead
produces thin slivers along *every* boundary of *every* district. For each
district we compute the intersection-over-union of the two vintages, the
area of their symmetric difference, the mean width of that symmetric
difference (its area divided by the district's perimeter), the number of
separate pieces it breaks into, and the largest single piece that is not
simply a change in the state's outline (coastline or state line).

```{r}
EA <- 5070  # USA Contiguous Albers Equal Area, for areas and lengths in m

compare_vintages <- function(a, b) {
  a <- st_transform(st_make_valid(a), EA)
  b <- st_transform(st_make_valid(b), EA)
  outline_change <- st_sym_difference(st_union(a), st_union(b))
  # st_make_valid can return a GEOMETRYCOLLECTION; keep only the polygon parts
  to_poly <- function(g) {
    if (st_geometry_type(g) == "GEOMETRYCOLLECTION") st_union(st_collection_extract(g, "POLYGON")) else g
  }
  map_dfr(a$district, function(d) {
    ga <- to_poly(st_geometry(a)[a$district == d])
    gb <- to_poly(st_geometry(b)[b$district == d])
    sd <- st_union(st_sym_difference(ga, gb))
    internal <- if (length(outline_change) && !all(st_is_empty(outline_change))) {
      st_union(st_difference(sd, outline_change))
    } else sd
    pieces <- if (length(internal) == 1 && !st_is_empty(internal)) {
      st_cast(suppressWarnings(st_collection_extract(internal, "POLYGON")), "POLYGON")
    } else st_sfc(crs = EA)
    area <- function(g) sum(as.numeric(st_area(g)))
    tibble(
      district      = d,
      iou           = area(st_intersection(ga, gb)) / area(st_union(ga, gb)),
      symdiff_km2   = area(sd) / 1e6,
      mean_width_m  = area(sd) / sum(as.numeric(st_length(st_boundary(ga)))),
      n_pieces      = length(pieces),
      largest_piece_km2 = if (length(pieces)) max(as.numeric(st_area(pieces))) / 1e6 else 0
    )
  }) |>
    mutate(outline_change_km2 = as.numeric(st_area(outline_change)) / 1e6)
}
```

### New Jersey, 103rd-105th vs. 106th-107th

```{r}
nj_cmp <- compare_vintages(nj_a, nj_b)
nj_cmp |> mutate(across(-district, \(x) round(x, 3))) |> print(n = Inf)
```

Every one of the 13 districts differs, by a sliver averaging a few tens of
meters wide broken into well over a hundred pieces, and the largest piece
of territory that actually changes district is under one square kilometer.
Only District 13 (`r sprintf("%.3f", nj_cmp$iou[nj_cmp$district == 13])`)
falls below the 0.99 merge threshold, which is why the two vintages were
never joined. The largest *outline* changes are tidal marsh along Delaware
Bay in Salem and Cumberland counties.

### Texas, 105th-106th vs. 107th

```{r}
tx_cmp <- compare_vintages(tx_a, tx_b)
tx_cmp |> mutate(across(-district, \(x) round(x, 3))) |> print(n = Inf)
```

Same signature across all 30 districts: slivers roughly 20-45 m wide,
hundreds to thousands of pieces, no single internal piece bigger than about
7 km^2 (and those few are rural West Texas county-line realignments in
Districts 13, 17, and 19 -- districts the *Vera* court never touched).
The large outline changes are the New Mexico state line, Matagorda Bay,
the Red River, and the Rio Grande.

### The same pattern in Census's own files

As an independent check, the Census Bureau's archived generalized
congressional district files
(<https://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/PREVGENZ/cd/>) can be compared the
same way between consecutive Congresses. If the Census had recorded a
redistricting, its own files would show whole-block transfers.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| results: hide
census_cd <- function(state_fips, cong) {
  zip <- sprintf("cd%s_%03i_shp.zip", state_fips, cong)
  url <- sprintf("https://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/PREVGENZ/cd/cd%03ishp/%s", cong, zip)
  dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "census_cd", tools::file_path_sans_ext(zip))
  if (!dir.exists(dir)) {
    dir.create(dir, recursive = TRUE)
    download.file(url, file.path(dir, zip), mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
    unzip(file.path(dir, zip), exdir = dir)
  }
  shp <- list.files(dir, pattern = "\\.shp$", full.names = TRUE)[1]
  x <- st_read(shp, quiet = TRUE)
  cd_col <- grep("^CD[0-9]*$", names(x), ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)[1]
  st_set_crs(x, 4269) |>
    st_transform(EA) |>
    mutate(district = suppressWarnings(as.integer(.data[[cd_col]]))) |>
    filter(!is.na(district)) |>   # drop non-district (water) polygons
    group_by(district) |>
    summarize(geometry = st_union(geometry), .groups = "drop") |>
    arrange(district)
}
tx_census_cmp <- compare_vintages(census_cd("48", 106), census_cd("48", 107))
nj_census_cmp <- compare_vintages(census_cd("34", 105), census_cd("34", 106))
```

```{r}
tx_census_cmp |> mutate(across(-district, \(x) round(x, 3))) |> print(n = Inf)
```

Census's own 106th- and 107th-Congress Texas files show essentially the
same sliver-everywhere pattern (the 107th file is in the Census 2000-era
cartographic boundary layout, i.e. it was regenerated from the new line
work). Nothing resembling a district-to-district transfer.

```{r}
nj_census_cmp |> mutate(across(-district, \(x) round(x, 3))) |> print(n = Inf)
```

For New Jersey, Census's generalized 105th and 106th files are nearly
identical to each other: the only differences are two sub-square-kilometer
pieces (one of them open water in Raritan Bay), confirming there was no
redistricting between the two Congresses.

## Fix

Merge each pair into a single range. Following the convention of
`dedup_districts()` in `R/dedup.R` (which keeps the latest vintage's
geometry, `geometry[n()]`, when it joins consecutive Congresses), the
merged files use the later vintage's shapes. All non-geometry attributes
other than the Congress range and the derived `id` are identical between
the two vintages, which we check first.

```{r}
attr_cols <- function(x) st_drop_geometry(x) |> select(-startcong, -endcong, -id)
stopifnot(identical(attr_cols(nj_a), attr_cols(nj_b)))
stopifnot(identical(attr_cols(tx_a), attr_cols(tx_b)))
```

```{r}
append_rnote <- function(x, text) {
  x |> mutate(rnote = if_else(
    rnote == "",
    sprintf('{"%s"}', text),
    str_replace(rnote, "\\}$", paste0(',"', text, '"}'))
  ))
}

merge_vintages <- function(later, state_fips, first_cong, last_cong, note) {
  later |>
    mutate(startcong = first_cong, endcong = last_cong) |>
    mutate(id = sprintf("%03i%03i%03i%03i", state_fips, startcong, endcong, district)) |>
    append_rnote(note) |>
    arrange(district)
}

nj_note <- paste(
  "GitHub issue #36 (see Patches/12-merge_nj_tx_vintages_issue36): the",
  "103rd-105th and 106th-107th Congress shapes differed only by Census",
  "TIGER line-vintage slivers and coastline realignment, not by any",
  "redistricting (no New Jersey plan changed between 1992 and 2002).",
  "Merged into one 103rd-107th range using the later vintage's geometry."
)
tx_note <- paste(
  "GitHub issue #36 (see Patches/12-merge_nj_tx_vintages_issue36): the",
  "105th-106th and 107th Congress shapes differed only by Census TIGER",
  "line-vintage slivers and coastline/state-line realignment, not by any",
  "redistricting (the 1996 Vera v. Bush interim plan stayed in force",
  "through the 2000 election). Merged into one 105th-107th range using",
  "the later vintage's geometry."
)

new_nj <- merge_vintages(nj_b, 34, 103, 107, nj_note)
new_tx <- merge_vintages(tx_b, 48, 105, 107, tx_note)
```

## Validate

```{r}
validate <- function(x, n_expected, state_fips) {
  x$statefp_code <- state_fips
  print(as_tibble(st_drop_geometry(x))[, c("district", "startcong", "endcong", "id")], n = Inf)
  stopifnot(nrow(x) == n_expected)
  stopifnot(all(x$district == seq_len(n_expected)))
  stopifnot(all(x$id == sprintf("%03i%03i%03i%03i", x$statefp_code, x$startcong, x$endcong, x$district)))
  stopifnot(all(st_is_valid(x)))
  # no pairwise overlap between districts beyond boundary noise
  xp <- st_transform(x, EA)
  combos <- combn(nrow(xp), 2)
  max_overlap <- max(map_dbl(seq_len(ncol(combos)), function(i) {
    sum(as.numeric(st_area(st_intersection(st_geometry(xp)[combos[1, i]],
                                           st_geometry(xp)[combos[2, i]]))))
  }))
  cat("max pairwise overlap (m^2):", max_overlap, "\n")
  stopifnot(max_overlap < 1)
  invisible(x)
}
validate(new_nj, 13, 34)
validate(new_tx, 30, 48)
```

Thirteen New Jersey districts and thirty Texas districts, all valid, with
no overlap between districts, and unchanged geometry relative to the later
vintage file each one replaces.

## Write out the merged files

```{r}
unlink("../../GeoJson/New Jersey_103_to_105.geojson")
unlink("../../GeoJson/New Jersey_106_to_107.geojson")
st_write(new_nj, "../../GeoJson/New Jersey_103_to_107.geojson", append = FALSE)

unlink("../../GeoJson/Texas_105_to_106.geojson")
unlink("../../GeoJson/Texas_107_to_107.geojson")
st_write(new_tx, "../../GeoJson/Texas_105_to_107.geojson", append = FALSE)
```

```{r}
list.files("../../GeoJson", pattern = "^(New Jersey|Texas)_1(0[3-9]|1[0-2])_to_")
```

New Jersey now goes 099-102, 103-107, 108-112 and Texas 103-104, 105-107,
108, 109, 110-112 -- one file per plan actually in force, with no gaps or
overlaps in Congress coverage.
